attributes.description:
Distribution opsdir-adapter-aws (import opsdir_adapter_aws), registered via entry point opsdir.adapters:aws; depends on opsdir, opsdir-adapter-x509, opsdir-format-terraform, opsdir-format-cloudformation and pyyaml.
- Network: VPC/subnet data, security groups.
- Landing zone: plumbing (NAT, route tables, NACLs, peering, transit, VPN, flow logs), OIDC deployer roles, Identity Center permission sets, SCP guardrails.
- Compute: EC2 instances and Auto Scaling groups.
- Edge: NLBs, ALBs with WAFv2 and Shield, CloudFront (from the standard account in GovCloud), Route 53 and Resolver rules, VPC endpoints, Network Firewall allowlists.
- Data: RDS and Aurora, S3, EBS, DLM, AWS Backup.
- Identity: IAM roles.
- Security: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Inspector, Config, Security Hub, Macie, suppressions.
- Observability: CloudWatch alarms and log groups, Synthetics canaries, Fluent Bit on EKS.
- Budgets.
- PKI: AWS Private CA inventory (private_ca.py, private_ca_access.py: CAs with state/key/parent, endpoints, audit-report templates with who may request from IAM, resource policy and ACM, audit-report certificates).
- Importers: aws/terraform-state, aws/cli-inventory, aws/cloudformation, aws/regions, aws/quotas, aws/private-ca. Collectors for the first three and aws/private-ca (read-only; never creates an audit report).
- Planner checks: boundary, regulated placement, discovery availability, server inputs.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["terraform CLI (applies the rendered roots; terraform state pull for collect --terraform-dir)", "hashicorp/aws Terraform provider (~> 6.68)", "hashicorp/archive Terraform provider (~> 2.8; canary and Macie scheduler packaging)", "AWS CloudFormation (render target cloudformation; stacks read by aws/cloudformation)", "AWS CLI (aws-sm resolution, opsdir collect, aws/regions and aws/quotas runs)", "amazon.aws Ansible collection (secretsmanager_secret lookup via opsdir-adapter-ansible)", "Amazon CloudWatch agent and aws-for-fluent-bit (configured, not installed)", "AWS Load Balancer Controller (TargetGroupBinding for cluster gateways)", "cfn-lint (CloudFormation validation script and tests only)"]
attributes.purpose:
Amazon Web Services provider adapter (ciamCloudProvider aws, ciamCloudEnvironment public; a us-gov-* ciamRegion selects GovCloud (US) and the aws-us-gov partition).
- Renders an environment's infrastructure bindings as Terraform for hashicorp/aws, or as AWS CloudFormation translated from the same Terraform data; what CloudFormation can't express stays in a Terraform root.
- Reads them back from Terraform state, AWS CLI JSON and CloudFormation stacks, and collects all three read-only under the operator's AWS CLI login.
- Owns the aws-sm, aws-kms, aws-acm and s3 reference schemes and refuses AWS credential forms.
- Supplies the AWS access model, EKS IRSA and secret delivery, CloudWatch agent host files, and region and quota prerequisites.

attributes.description:
Distribution opsdir-adapter-gcp (import opsdir_adapter_gcp), registered via entry point opsdir.adapters:gcp; depends on opsdir, opsdir-adapter-x509 and opsdir-format-terraform.
- Network: Shared VPC network data; firewall rules by network tag, or a network firewall policy by secure tag; Private Service Connect; egress allowlists.
- Landing zone: plumbing (Cloud NAT, routes, peering, HA VPN), workload identity federation, org-policy guardrails, Assured Workloads, budgets.
- Compute: Compute Engine instances and regional managed instance groups.
- Edge: passthrough and Application load balancers with Cloud Armor, Cloud CDN and Cloud DNS.
- Data: Cloud SQL, buckets, disks, snapshot schedules, Backup and DR.
- Identity: service accounts and IAM members.
- Security: audit sinks, Security Command Center, Compliance Manager, mute rules, Sensitive Data Protection.
- Observability: alert policies, log buckets and sinks, uptime checks, synthetic monitors.
- PKI: Certificate Authority Service inventory (private_ca.py, private_ca_access.py: pools' CAs with state/key/parent, endpoints, the pool policy and templates as the CA's own with who may request from pool/template/project IAM, an Enterprise pool's certificates).
- Importers: gcp/terraform-state, gcp/cli-inventory, gcp/regions, gcp/quotas, gcp/frameworks, gcp/private-ca.
- Collectors: cli-inventory, terraform-state, private-ca.
- Planner checks: priorities, boundary, regulated placement, server inputs, discovery cadence.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["terraform CLI (applies the rendered roots; terraform state pull for collect --terraform-dir)", "hashicorp/google Terraform provider (~> 8.6)", "hashicorp/archive Terraform provider (~> 2.8; synthetic monitor source packaging)", "gcloud CLI (gcp-sm resolution, opsdir collect, gcp/regions, gcp/quotas and gcp/frameworks runs, Policy Troubleshooter in access/evaluate.sh)", "Google Cloud Ops Agent (configured, not installed)"]
attributes.purpose:
Google Cloud provider adapter (ciamCloudProvider gcp, ciamCloudEnvironment public).
- Renders an environment's infrastructure bindings as Terraform for hashicorp/google, in platform, landing-zone and per-keeper roots.
- Reads them back from Terraform state and from Cloud Asset Inventory and gcloud JSON, and collects both read-only under the operator's gcloud login.
- Owns the gcp-sm, gcp-kms, gcp-cert and gs reference schemes (gcp-sm resolved with gcloud) and refuses Google Cloud credential forms.
- Supplies the Google Cloud access model, GKE workload identity and secret delivery, Ops Agent host files, region, quota and compliance-framework prerequisites, and Assured Workloads boundary checks.

attributes.description: opsdir-adapter-x509 (kind pki, declaration-only): plan.py (what each endpoint is asked: CRL URLs, OCSP GET requests with a SHA-1 CertID, no nonce, one serial from core revocation.probe_serial), collect.py (estate collector of observing Requests), verify.py (CRL and OCSP response parsing and signature checks: CA-signed, delegated responder with id-kp-OCSPSigning; PSS OCSP unsupported), revocation.py (importer x509/revocation replacing ou=revocation-observations), certificates.py (CA-neutral certificate_facts for CA importers), reasons.py (CA products' revocation reason names as RFC 5280 codes and names: AWS Private CA, Google CAS). The only package depending on cryptography.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["cryptography>=50.0.2 (pyca; CRL/OCSP parsing, signature verification, OCSP request building)"]
attributes.purpose: The X.509 standards (RFC 5280 CRLs, RFC 6960 OCSP), CA-neutral: every recorded CA's revocation endpoints observed read-only and checked against the CA certificates the record holds, into the core pki domain's revocation observations

attributes.name: authority_entry
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory"}, {"name": "name", "type": "str"}, {"name": "provider_ref", "type": "str|None"}, {"name": "templates", "type": "tuple"}, {"name": "facts", "type": "dict|None", "required": false, "description": "{attribute of AUTHORITY_FACTS: value or None}; ciamParentAuthority given as the parent CA's name; None: not read (those attributes not owned)"}]
attributes.purpose: Importer builder: a ciamCertAuthority entry (provider ref, published templates and, when given, what the CA's product says of it: AUTHORITY_FACTS type/state/key algorithm/storage/key ref/parent CA), operator attributes kept

attributes.name: authority_rows
attributes.purpose: certificate-authorities report rows: config, state (CA type and state), key (algorithm, storage, key ref), issued by (hierarchy; else the product's parent CA), CA certificates, templates, endpoints, inventory, owner

attributes.name: revocation_code
attributes.purpose: The RFC 5280 CRLReason code a CA product's revocation reason name stands for (AWS Private CA / Google CAS enum names, RFC names; case and separators ignored), or None when it names none.

attributes.name: reason_name
attributes.purpose: The RFC 5280 reason name the record writes (ciamRevocationReason) for a product's reason name: unspecified when none is given, the product's name as it is when it matches no RFC reason.

attributes.name: statement_grant
attributes.purpose: What one IAM policy statement says of an action on a resource (Action/NotAction, Resource/NotResource, IAM wildcards): None, ('all', None), ('only'|'except', acm-pca:TemplateArn patterns) or ('unknown', why) for any other condition.

attributes.name: access
attributes.purpose: 'yes', 'no' or 'unknown': whether policy documents (None for one not held) allow the action on the resource with a template; an applicable unconditional or template deny wins.

attributes.name: principals
attributes.purpose: ((principal ARN, its policy documents; None for a managed policy the export doesn't hold), ...) of a get-account-authorization-details answer: each user (with its groups' policies) and each role.

attributes.name: resource_policy_enrollees
attributes.purpose: ((enrollee, broad), ...) and whether any statement is unknown, of a CA's resource policy for a template: every principal ('*') and other accounts broad, the account's own principals named.

attributes.name: acm_grants
attributes.purpose: Whether a CA's list-permissions answer lets ACM (acm.amazonaws.com) issue from it.

attributes.name: enrollment
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "iam", "type": "dict|None", "required": true}, {"name": "policy", "type": "str|None", "required": true}, {"name": "permissions", "type": "dict|None", "required": true}, {"name": "ca_arn", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "account", "type": "str|None", "required": true}, {"name": "template", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "through_acm", "type": "bool", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: (enrollees, scope broad|restricted|unknown, why unknown or None) of a CA's template: principals the account's IAM lets issue from it, the CA resource policy's, and (when ACM issues from it) principals allowed acm:RequestCertificate (through ACM).

attributes.name: ca_id
attributes.purpose: A Private CA ARN's id, or None.

attributes.name: arn_part
attributes.purpose: The n-th colon-separated part of an ARN (1 partition, 3 region, 4 account), or None.

attributes.name: template_name
attributes.purpose: An AWS Private CA template ARN's name (EndEntityCertificate/V1), any partition, or None.

attributes.name: template_usages
attributes.purpose: The extended key usage OIDs AWS fixes for a template by its family (FAMILY_USAGES); () for Blank* and CA templates.

attributes.name: endpoints
attributes.purpose: ((kind, n, url, template or None), ...) a CA writes into what it issues: its CRL distribution point (S3 bucket host or CustomCname, CustomPath; partitioned kept as a template; none when the extension is omitted) and OCSP responder (AWS's or OcspCustomCname).

attributes.name: ca_name
attributes.purpose: A Private CA's record name: its certificate's subject CN, else its configured subject's, else its id.

attributes.name: report_time
attributes.purpose: (GeneralizedTime, datetime) of the newest audit report an audit-report listing names, or (None, None).

attributes.name: issued_facts
attributes.purpose: The ciamIssuedCertificate facts of an audit report row (serial hex, subject, validity, the CA's own template, ACM requester, revocation time and RFC reason; no fingerprint), or None without a serial.

attributes.name: inventory_state
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "get", "type": "callable", "required": true, "description": "name -> the CA folder's file text or None"}, {"name": "arn", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "region", "type": "str|None", "required": true}, {"name": "at", "type": "datetime", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: (state, problems, GeneralizedTime of the inventory, report rows) of a CA's audit reports: complete when the newest is less than FRESH older than the read; incomplete when stale or missing, naming the create command (the CA owner's).

attributes.name: read_ca
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "ca", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "get", "type": "callable", "required": true}, {"name": "iam", "type": "dict|None", "required": true}, {"name": "by_subject", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "at", "type": "datetime", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: (Imported groups, notices) of one Private CA: its entry with AWS's facts (type, state, key algorithm/storage, parent) and endpoints, its inventory from the newest audit report, the templates that report shows as its own with who may request.

attributes.name: read_private_ca
attributes.purpose: Importer aws/private-ca read(): per CA the account owns, its entry, endpoints, inventory and templates, each replacing the record's; shared CAs named; refused without --at.

attributes.name: report_bucket
attributes.purpose: The audit-report bucket environment m's aws/private-ca collection source names (s3://<bucket>), or None.

attributes.name: private_ca_steps
attributes.purpose: Collector steps for aws/private-ca: the CA listings (owned, shared) and the account's IAM policies (projected), then each owned CA's certificate, resource policy, ACM permission and, with a report bucket, its audit-report listing and newest report; read-only, never creates a report.

attributes.name: private_ca_problems
attributes.purpose: Collector.problems of aws/private-ca: a collection source naming no bucket (s3://<bucket>), or more than one source.

attributes.name: is_broad
attributes.purpose: Whether an IAM member is a broad group: allUsers, allAuthenticatedUsers or a whole domain (domain:).

attributes.name: holders
attributes.purpose: (members holding one of the roles unconditionally, members whose binding can't be judged: conditional or a custom role) of IAM policies (None for one not read).

attributes.name: enrollment
attributes.purpose: (enrollees, scope broad|restricted|unknown, why unknown or None) of requesting from a CA pool (certificates.create via pool or project IAM), with a template when templated (templates.use via template or project IAM; a broad side admits the other side's members).

attributes.name: resource_part
attributes.purpose: The id after <collection>/ in a Google resource name (projects/p/locations/l/caPools/x, caPools -> x), or None.

attributes.name: x509_usages
attributes.purpose: The extended key usage OIDs CAS X509Parameters set (extendedKeyUsage flags and unknownExtendedKeyUsages).

attributes.name: passes_usages
attributes.purpose: Whether a request may pass its own extended key usages through (a passthroughExtensions naming EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE).

attributes.name: names_subject
attributes.purpose: Whether the requester names the subject: unless every identity constraint given forbids subject and SAN passthrough (none given: allowed).

attributes.name: lifetime_days
attributes.purpose: The smallest maximum lifetime ('2592000s') in whole days rounded up, or None when none is set.

attributes.name: template_facts
attributes.purpose: (subject from request, extended key usages, longest validity days) of a pool's issuance policy, combined with a certificate template's when given.

attributes.name: ca_endpoints
attributes.purpose: ((kind, n, url, None), ...) a CAS CA writes into what it issues: its CRL and CA certificate URLs (user-defined, else published) and its pool's baseline OCSP servers.

attributes.name: ca_facts
attributes.purpose: What Google says of a CA (AUTHORITY_FACTS): type, state, key algorithm, storage (Google-managed HSM / Cloud KMS key), key reference, parent (subordinateConfig, else by issuer subject, else the record's CA by issuer CN).

attributes.name: ca_name
attributes.purpose: A CAS CA's record name: its certificate's subject CN, else its id.

attributes.name: issued_facts
attributes.purpose: The ciamIssuedCertificate facts of a CAS certificate from its public PEM (certificate_facts), its template as the CA's own (<CA>/<pool>[/<template>]), its revocation by RFC name; None without a certificate.

attributes.name: read_ca
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "ca", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "pool", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "certs", "type": "tuple|None", "required": true}, {"name": "templates", "type": "tuple", "required": true}, {"name": "policies", "type": "tuple", "required": true, "description": "(project IAM, pool IAM, template id -> template IAM)"}, {"name": "names", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "by_subject", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "at", "type": "str", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: (Imported groups, notices) of one CA of a pool: its entry with Google's facts and endpoints, its inventory (the pool's certificates it issued; DevOps or unread listing incomplete) and its own templates.

attributes.name: read_pool
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "pool", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "get", "type": "callable", "required": true}, {"name": "location_get", "type": "callable", "required": true}, {"name": "project_policy", "type": "dict|None", "required": true}, {"name": "names", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "by_subject", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "at", "type": "str", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: (Imported groups, notices) of one CA pool: each of its root and subordinate CAs (read_ca).

attributes.name: read_private_ca
attributes.purpose: Importer gcp/private-ca read(): per CA of the project's pools its entry, endpoints, inventory and own templates, each replacing the record's; refused without --at.

attributes.name: certificate_fields
attributes.purpose: A Command keep function: gcloud privateca certificates list output with each certificate only CERTIFICATE_FIELDS (no CSR, config or description).

attributes.name: private_ca_steps
attributes.purpose: Collector steps for gcp/private-ca: pools (every location) and project IAM, then per pool its roots, subordinates, IAM and (not DevOps) trimmed certificates, per location its templates, then each template's IAM; read-only.

attributes.description: Milestone 108 item (e), cloud private CAs (task 559 said they wait for task 557's merge: done). Read AWS Private CA (opsdir-adapter-aws) and Google Cloud Certificate Authority Service (opsdir-adapter-gcp) into the CA-neutral pki model (flow 60), metadata only, never keys: CAs (hierarchy, key algorithm/storage, status), CA pools/templates as CA-scoped templates (ciamTemplateAuthority), revocation configuration (CRL distribution/S3/GCS, OCSP), and the issued certificates the service records (AWS: no list-certificates API: the audit report written to S3; Google: ListCertificates per pool). Read-only collectors with least privilege (exact IAM actions/roles), saved-export importers (pure), certificate parsing via opsdir-adapter-x509 certificate_facts. GovCloud / Assured Workloads availability checked on each vendor's government-cloud page as well as the general one; report disagreements. Use the existing core pki model and GET-only collection; if a core pki change seems needed, escalate to the master first (task 562's worker owns core pki this round). Azure Key Vault certificates are a managed inventory: they wait for task 562's concept (deferred note). Tests, showcase change, README/docs. Reserved: core attrs 910-919, classes 197-198; showcase CHG-2122..2124, A286-A291, B114-B116.
